reasoning: Missouri has no U.S. Senate or gubernatorial election in 2026, so there are no state-specific 2026 general-election Senate or presidential polls to establish a current D+ or R+ margin; the only directly relevant structural indicator is the statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index of about R+9, reflecting the state’s strong Republican lean.[11][7] Recent Missouri coverage over the last 45 days focuses on state legislative primaries, statewide ballot measures, and House races, none of which measure the statewide 2026 general-election Senate or presidential contests, so they cannot be used as direct evidence of a current margin for those races.[1][2][5][9][10][14][15] Given this lack of state-specific 2026 general-election polling for Senate or president, the best available characterization is that Missouri structurally favors Republicans by roughly 9 points, but there is no current polling-based margin for a 2026 statewide Senate or presidential race.
